overview.headline: DNA sequencing reads bases to reveal genes and guide health research

keyPoints.point: Sequencing DNA means reading the order of chemical building blocks that make up genetic segments.
keyPoints.quote: Sequencing DNA means determining the order of the four chemical building blocks - called "bases" - that make up the DNA molecule.

keyPoints.point: Adenine always pairs with thymine while cytosine always pairs with guanine in the double helix.
keyPoints.quote: Adenine (A) always pairs with thymine (T); cytosine (C) always pairs with guanine (G).

keyPoints.point: The human genome contains about 3 billion base pairs with instructions for making and maintaining a human being.
keyPoints.quote: The human genome contains about 3 billion base pairs that spell out the instructions for making and maintaining a human being.

keyPoints.point: Researchers compare large stretches of DNA from different individuals quickly and cheaply to study inheritance and disease.
keyPoints.quote: Researchers now are able to compare large stretches of DNA - 1 million bases or more - from different individuals quickly and cheaply.
